name: Reassurance seeking (rate me threads)

lead: Rate-me threads are forum posts where people share photos and ask for ratings or critiques of their face. The payoff people want is an outside opinion on their attractiveness and a list of what to improve.

Users post photos and receive scores and feedback from other members. Clinically, repeatedly asking others to confirm how you look is described as a behaviour in body dysmorphic disorder, alongside mirror checking and comparing. No studies specific to these threads were found; related research links appearance-focused social media use to body dissatisfaction.

paras: People post front and side photos to a forum thread, read the ratings and comments, and use them to pick things to work on, such as grooming, fitness or skin. Some return repeatedly with updated photos to track changes.

Feedback comes from anonymous strangers and can be harsh. In BDD, repeated reassurance seeking tends to bring short-term relief followed by renewed doubt. Related research links appearance-focused social media use to body dissatisfaction.

angle.text: Rate-me threads give people outside opinions on facial attractiveness and ideas for what to improve. The same pattern, repeated reassurance seeking, is listed clinically among BDD behaviours, so feedback that helps one person plan can become a loop for another.

lead: A rate-me thread is a forum post in which a user shares photos and asks other members to rate or critique their face and features. On looksmaxxing forums such as looksmax.org, these threads are used to get a read on where someone stands and which features (skin, jaw, hair, body fat, posture) might be improved, so the poster can choose what to work on next.

Responses typically include a numeric score, comments on specific features, and a short list of suggestions. One looksmax.org reply to a teenage poster, for example, simply listed sport, diet, chin exercises and temporalis training as the route to improvement [1]. Many threads follow a title-and-age format with a tag such as "be brutal" requesting blunt feedback [2][3].

In clinical psychology, repeatedly asking others to confirm how one looks is called reassurance seeking and is described as one of the repetitive behaviors in body dysmorphic disorder, alongside mirror checking, comparing and camouflaging [4]. Research on appearance-related social comparison and on feedback seeking in social media exists, but no published study has examined rate-me threads themselves [5][6].

paras: A poster uploads front and side photos, often with age and height in the title, and asks for a rating. Replies commonly give a score on an informal scale and name features that hold the face back or stand out [1][2][3]. Some posters ask for "brutal" honesty or for advice on how to "ascend" [2][7].
Threads are usually short. Many receive a one-line rating and a suggestion; others attract extended feature-by-feature breakdowns.

Wikipedia describes reassurance seeking as a common behavior in body dysmorphic disorder, together with mirror checking, comparing and camouflaging. It also notes that heavy selfie-taking and social media use are linked to low self-esteem and body dysmorphic tendencies, with users sometimes seeking validation through likes and comments, and that a 2020 systematic review found appearance-focused social media use linked to body image dissatisfaction [4].

Related research examines appearance-related social comparison as a possible mechanism behind appearance-related psychopathology [5], and associations between social-media feedback seeking, popularity and depressive symptoms in adolescents [6]. Studies of reassurance seeking in obsessive-compulsive disorder compare it with compulsive checking [8]. These studies cover broader behaviors, not rate-me threads specifically.

Rate-me threads are a staple of looksmaxxing forums and are the usual first post from new members. Posters say they use the ratings to benchmark themselves and choose interventions; some threads include before-and-after follow-ups showing the effect of changes in grooming or fitness [1][2].

No studies found on rate-me threads. Cognitive-behavioral therapy for body dysmorphic disorder, which includes exposure and response prevention aimed at rituals such as reassurance seeking, has been tested in randomized trials [4].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, rate-me threads are treated as a routine way to get feedback and a starting list of features to improve.
